scene clearnightsky
So we head outside and hop into the first of many taxis positioned in a queue parallel to the valet parking lane which is, for some reason, still operating this late at night.

And still rather busy too. It seems like Sana chose a popular spot — which is one more aspect of her person that seems all the more different from the girl I remember in school, who could barely even look at me at first.
There’s a lot that’s different now, though. Even the people that line the streets have gone back to a more reasonable split of sexes now that those like me have descended.
And while I kind of wish that wasn’t the case, it’s for reasons you might not have expected this time.
Reasons that, conceptually, still revolve around jealousy and angst, but combine to make me seem like a good person rather than a bad one.
Am I good now, though? That’s the question I’ve been asking myself a lot these days.
Temptation isn’t so tempting anymore. I am present. And I am entirely dedicated to cultivating my own personal garden rather than propagating every plant I find out in the wild.
It’s working, too. We don’t argue. We don’t fight. We just exist in the same place, eat at the same table, and sleep within the confines of the same home.
If I was a religious man like my mother wished, I’d go so far as saying this might be Heaven.
Look — I capitalized the H and everything. I’m not overflowing with scorn or spite any longer. I’m ready to learn and willing to work.
The main reason I don’t call it Heaven, though, is because I’ve accepted this as reality.
I have reached the good ending. And I’ve reset in a way that, not so dissimilar from how it was when I woke up in Kumon-mi, has granted me a third chance at life.
And I will not make the same mistakes again — for I understand what it is I have to protect now.
scene black
And as I twist the key into the lock of my door once more, I find myself forcing back a smile rather than trying to remember how to don one for once.
Maybe that’s why I still look so young despite the passage of time? More...facial exercise or something like that?
Whatever the case, it’s not like any of this actually matters since your days are numbered now too — just as mine are.
You have no reason or desire to watch someone who isn’t struggling, do you?
I don’t blame you for that. Joy doesn’t hit the same way sorrow does — and I likely wouldn’t watch my own life right now either.
But that might just be because I’m too busy actually living it.
: Hima-chan! We’re home!
scene himadinner1
And that every second I spend watching something else would do naught but distract me from the first face I’ve ever known that makes all the misery in the world just melt away.
I really am a loser now, aren’t I?
: Sorry we’re late! We lost track of time with Sana and-
: Something feels off.
scene himadinner2
: Off? How do you mean?
: She normally greets us at the door.
: Akira, it’s like midnight. She’s probably just asleep.
: No...Something’s different. I don’t like it.
scene himadinner3
: Hima-chan! Are you awake?! Your father is having daughter withdrawal again and it’s making him be all negative on our anniversary!
scene himadinner4
: Okay...yeah. Something does feel different. I get what you mean now.
: She’d have told us if she went to a friend’s house, right?
: I’ll check her room. Maybe she just has her headphones on again or something?
scene black
: I’ll come with you.
: Akira, are we overbearing as parents? Do we dote on our daughter too much? Would a normal couple be this anxious like five seconds after walking into their own home?
: If something feels off, probably.
: Himawari, open up. We’re back from-
: Wait! Akira, look...
: What? What are you-
Ayane grabs me by the wrist and pulls me away from the door.
Past the bathroom.
Down the hall.
Into the living room.
And what we find is-
scene himadinner5
What we find is this.
: Wha...
: Did Hima-chan do all of this?...
scene himadinner6
: Did you put her up to it? Is this some sort of coordinated father-daughter surprise to try and make me love you more? Your acting’s gotten really good, Akira.
: I have nothing to do with this. I’m just as surprised as you.
: I’m currently too relieved to feel any happiness, though. So get back to me in a few minutes and ask me how I feel about it then.
scene himadinner7
: There’s a note too. Look.
scene himadinner8
: Happy anniversary...Your server will be with you shortly...
: Does she not know we literally just went out to eat?
scene himadinner9
: Oh no. I’m going to cry.
: Please don’t. That’ll make me want to cry and I’ve done such a good job my whole life at avoiding that.
scene himadinner10
: Nope! Here it comes! She’s too pure for this world, Akira! What did we do to deserve a daughter like her?!
: Mr. and Mrs. Arakawa — welcome to Chateau de L’Himawari. We’d like to extend our gratitude for you dining with us on such a special occasion.
scene himadinner11
: And now she’s in a tuxedo?! Akira, look! Hima-chan’s wearing a tuxedo! She’s so cute that I want to blow the house up! This is the greatest day of my life!
: I’m flattered, Mom. Really. But you might want to keep your voice down or you’re going to wake the entire neighborhood up.
: LET THEM WAKE UP! I DON’T CARE!
: Himawari...if we’d known you were going to do this, we wouldn’t have stayed out so late. You should’ve said something.
scene himadinner12
: And ruined the surprise? As if! I don’t mind staying up a little later than normal if it means getting to do something special for you two.
: A fancy dinner’s the least I can do to say thanks to you guys for literally creating me.
scene himadinner13
: Oh, and Aunt Sana helped too. Getting you guys out of the house long enough for me to set everything up would have been impossible without her.
: Plus, I’m not old enough to buy alcohol yet and I needed an adult for that since Dad doesn’t want me using my gun to intimidate shopkeepers.
: That goes against family tradition, though! It’s why I bought you a gun in the first place!
scene himadinner14
: Right? Like, maybe it’s just a girl thing because he clearly doesn’t get it.
: Yeah, silly me for not wanting my daughter flashing a firearm in public. Either way, you didn’t have to-
scene himadinner15
: Just scold me tomorrow if you have to! You only get one anniversary each year and it’s my job to make sure it’s a good one since you never remember the date!
scene himadinner16
: Now, with that out of the way, might I recommend this 1975 Chateau Margaux?
: Its mature and savory flavor profile with hints of tobacco, cloves, and bitter cherries give it a remarkable tannic firmness that makes it an exquisite pairing for both venison and wild game.
: I will drink anything you put in front of me.
: So you’re a sommelier now? Giving up on piano already?
scene himadinner17
: Not at all. It’s just easier to memorize pretentious wine descriptions off the Internet than it is to figure out VII. Cadenza I from Sorabji's “Opus Clavicembalisticum.”
: I’m proud you even figured out the pronunciation of whatever it is you just said. But even more proud of your father for managing to keep your brain from deteriorating as your new teacher.
scene himadinner18
: Dad’s a great teacher! I’ve literally never been happier. Plus, being a server-slash-sommelier is way more fun when I don’t have to worry about doing homework in between courses.
: There are courses?
scene himadinner19
: Two of them, to be precise. Wine and then dinner.
: You’re counting “wine” as a course?
: I’m about to count “whine” as a third one if you don’t stop your complaining already.
: What’s on the menu, Hima-chan? Assuming this isn’t a pre-prepared tasting menu of exactly one item.
scene himadinner20
: Tonight’s specials are as follows: brown-sugar glazed salmon with a Mediterranean vegetable medley, frozen garlic bread, and A-5 wagyu hamburg steak served with a red wine reduction.
: I feel like one of those things could have been left off the menu.
scene himadinner21
: Yeah, that wagyu really ate up most of the budget. Should’ve just gone with more garlic bread.
: I’ll have the salmon, Hima-chan. I’m sorry in advance if I can’t finish it, though. And also if I am drunk after one more glass of wine. We stayed at the hotel bar longer than I expected.
scene himadinner22
: No worries at all. Your orders have been taken and I will begin preparing them immediately.
: But I haven’t even ordered yet.
scene himadinner23
: The menu is more of a formality than anything. I know you want the hamburg steak and I knew Mom would want the salmon. I merely gave you the illusion of choice.
: Do you need help with anything? I’m obviously not a great cook, but I can at least-
: Dad — you’re not seriously planning on trying to help me do something nice for you guys, are you? I can cook. I don’t need you to chip in here.
: It just seems like a lot for-
: I am fine. Just relax and drink with Mom while I get started. Do yourself a favor and forget I’m even here.
: Easier said than done, Hima-chan. I’m second place in my own husband’s life now. Which really doesn’t hurt as much as I thought it would given that first place is obviously you.
scene himadinner24
: Well, that’s no good. You’ve gotta call it a tie at least, Dad. You can’t just let your daughter bias beat out your lifelong love for an amazing, beautiful woman.
: It is a tie.
: Then why am I not your wallpaper, hmm?
: I’m your wallpaper, Dad? Creepy.
: You should have seen what it was in high school.
: You should have seen when your mom made an exact replica of my phone, contacts and all, and kept it with her in the event that I lost mine.
scene himadinner25
: Okay, now that’s actually creepy. Not just the teasing kind where I make fun of Dad for loving me so much.
: We all do creepy things in the name of love, Hima-chan. I also took pictures of him while he was sleeping, framed them, and hung them above my bed.
: Who are you all of a sudden?
: It’s not “all of a sudden.” This is who I’ve always been. Look — I have sleeping photos of you too.
scene himadinner26
: What the- don’t show me those! You’re making even Dad look normal right now!
scene himadinner27

: Just...drink your wine! And ignore the fact that I’m going to be in and out of this kitchen over the next ten to fifteen minutes while I grab stuff out of the fridge to prepare your food in my room.
: Your room? Why are you cooking in your room? Just use the kitchen.
: And interrupt your private anniversary dinner where you talk about weird adult stuff with each other? Nooooooo thank you! I’ll be over here — remaining pure.
: Is that what you think we talk about while you’re not around?
: I try not to think about that at all actually. Now, ignore me! I’m no longer here!
scene himadinner28
Himawari, with her arms full of ingredients, swings her door shut with her foot and leaves Ayane and me in the living room to try and wrap our heads around how lucky we are to have her.
And Sana apparently. Who, ignoring the fact that she may have propositioned me to have an affair with her earlier, helped make this dream a reality as well.
To think we’d ever end up here, though — so shamelessly happy despite the scars and the trauma and all that we’ve lost...
Well, to think that we’d be anywhere close to here just makes all of the pain worth it.
scene himadinner29
scene himadinner30
It’s definitely worth it...
This is the future I was meant to end up with.
I have no regrets at all...
: It really doesn’t feel like 1:00 AM, does it?
: Yeah. It’s technically not even our anniversary anymore.
scene himadinner31
: Well, whatever you do, don’t let Hima-chan hear you say that. Not after all the trouble she must have gone through to make this happen.
: It’s kind of funny, though. A few weeks ago, she asked me to teach her how to make hamburg steak and I didn’t think anything of it. Just thought it was a craving.
: I should have ordered the frozen garlic bread instead and thrown her off her game. She’s become too powerful, Ayane.
scene himadinner32
: Right?! Like, how are we supposed to look at her and not want to just...squeeze her until she explodes?!
: There’s no way all parents feel this way, right? Like, this has gotta be an “us” thing.
: I think we’re both living examples of how not all parents feel this way, Ayane.
scene himadinner33
: Well...true.
: But...
: But what? What’s with that solemn, contemplative look all of a sudden? Don’t let Himawari catch wind of that either or she’ll scold us for not having enough fun again.
: It’s just...
scene himadinner34
: Well, you’ve ”remembered” some stuff right? About all the time we missed when we woke up here?
: You mean, like...memories from stuff we weren’t exactly present for?
: Exactly. How there will be, like...faint traces of things you just sort of know, but can’t quite understand why or how.
: Sure. Plenty of stuff that I do for the first time here feels familiar. Is that what you mean?
: Yeah. But, like...
: Even with all of that. All of that stuff that I just know now-
: I still don’t really know anything about your parents.
: Which is fine. I don’t need to. I just...figured you’d have mentioned something by now since we’ve been together for so long.
: Ahh. Yeah, it’d probably feel weird for me if I was forced into the same boat.
: Were they really that bad? That you’d just...block them out?
: I don’t really know.
: What?
: Like...maybe? They’d kind of need to be for me to...grow the way I did. Just the details are so sparing that it feels like thinking about them at all is a waste of time.
: That doesn’t always stop me, though. Like, just a little while ago, a stray thought about my mother found its way back to me.
: What kind of thought? If you don’t mind telling me, of course.
: Just that I’d be a bit of a disappointment now. That’s all.
scene himadinner35
: What? What’s that look?
: A serious one. That doesn’t pretend to understand you, but wants you to know that I don’t think you’re a disappointment.
: I think you’re amazing. And handsome. And a better father and husband than either of us would have ever imagined.
: I don’t know enough about your parents to hate them. And I don’t really know if you hate them either. Just...
: I’m also thankful. Because I’d still be incomplete if it wasn’t for them.
: I’m thankful to your parents for the same reason.
: I do know enough to hate them, though.
scene himadinner36
: Heh...At least we have Geoffrey, right?
: Think he’s willing to adopt me this late into both of our lives?
: It might interfere with our marriage license, but I’ll see what I can do.
: Want to invite him over for Christmas? It’s been a while, hasn’t it?
scene himadinner37
: You wouldn’t mind?
: Not at all. He’s basically always been your actual father as far as I’m concerned.
scene himadinner38
: Maybe I’ll give him a call then.
: Let’s table this for now, though. Dinner approaches.
scene himadinner39
: Mr. and Mrs. Arakawa — apologies for the delay. Cooking with a hotplate on one’s computer desk is not as easy as it sounds.
: Regardless, dinner is served. Will either of you be requiring another glass of Chateau Margaux?
: I’m okay for now, Hima-chan. I’ve barely touched the first one.
: You’re done cooking already? That felt quick.
scene himadinner40
: Service is faster when the entire restaurant is reserved for two, Mr. Arakawa. There’s no way these dishes were made beforehand and merely heated up, if that’s what you’re suggesting.
: ...Well, it wasn’t. But now that you mention it-
: Please hold that thought while I retrieve an even stronger bottle of wine from the cellar. The Margaux doesn’t pair well with fish, you see.
: Before you go, there’s something else.
scene himadinner41
: Any other complaints can be submitted through our website. The manager is far too busy right now to-
: I just wanted to say thank you. For all of this.
scene himadinner42
: Huh?
: Dinner. It’s an amazing gesture and an even better surprise.
: Thank you for making our lives better in every possible way.
scene himadinner43
: Wha-
: We love you, Himawari. More than anything.
scene himadinner44
: S...Stop embarrassing the wait staff! They have a job to do!
scene black
Dinner is delicious, even if it’s just reheated.
There’s a not-so-secret ingredient in every single bite.
